question.problem:
$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $B$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\lambda =-5$ is an eigenvalue of $B$

II. $\lambda =-1$ is an eigenvalue of $B$

III. The eigenvalue $\lambda =-3$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd column, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-5-\lambda )\cdot (-3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )\cdot (-3-\lambda )((3-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )+10) & =0 \\ (\lambda +5)(\lambda +3)({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $D<0$ for the polynomial ${\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +7$, we have that the only real eigenvalues are $\lambda =-5$ and $\lambda =-3$ (both with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
